raw_response:
I've been farming these 20 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. I'm 60 this year, and my legs aren't what they used to be, but I still know every piece of this land. Middle school education, so I can read the extension leaflets, but honestly I trust what I've seen with my own eyes more than what some young technician tells me. Six people at home — my wife, my son and daughter-in-law, two grandkids. We mostly rely on family labor, though I hire a custom planter for the maize because that week after wheat harvest is murder.

I split my 20 mu like this: **10 mu for wheat-maize double cropping**, **5 mu for cotton**, and **5 mu for chili**. I thought about dropping the cotton last year because the price was shaky, but my neighbor Lao Wang did okay, so I'm keeping it. The chili has been good money when the price is right, though it kills your back with all the picking.

**The wheat** is already in the ground from last October — I used an improved local variety, not the fanciest hybrid but reliable. I put down base fertilizer in the fall, about 15 kg per mu of compound fertilizer. Now it's greening up and looks a bit yellow in patches. I'll topdress 10 kg of urea per mu at green-up, and if it still looks hungry at jointing, another 5 kg. Three irrigations: green-up, jointing, and flowering. The pump electricity isn't cheap — about 25 yuan per mu per watering — so I don't waste water. I sprayed herbicide last fall, so weeds aren't too bad. Expecting around 420 kg per mu if we don't get a late frost.

**Summer maize** goes in right after wheat harvest, usually June 8-12. I have maybe five days, so I hire the planter tractor — 40 yuan per mu. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or something similar, about 45 yuan per mu. At planting I put 15 kg per mu of compound fertilizer. Then at the big trumpet stage I'll side-dress 8 kg of urea, assuming I have the cash. Two irrigations: one if it's dry at planting, one at flowering. I don't usually spray much pesticide on maize, maybe a little herbicide. Hoping for 480 kg per mu.

**Cotton** on 5 mu, planted mid-April. Seed cost is about 25 yuan per mu. I plow and harrow good before planting — cotton hates compacted soil. Fertilizer is about 14 kg N per mu total: base compound fertilizer plus a flowering topdress. Two irrigations, at flowering and boll stage. Bollworm is the enemy, so I spray insecticide two or three times. I'll pick most of it myself and family, but might hire 2-3 days of labor for the second picking if we're busy. Expecting 280 kg per mu of seed cotton.

**Chili** on 5 mu. I start seedlings in late March in the backyard, transplant in early May. I ridge the soil and use plastic mulch — keeps moisture in and weeds down. Fertilizer is about 12 kg N plus extra potassium, since chili needs it. Four irrigations, especially when the fruit is setting. Aphids are the main problem, so insecticide, and sometimes fungus if it's wet. This is the most labor-intensive crop — my wife and daughter-in-law do most of the picking. Yield maybe 300 kg per mu of dry chili if we're lucky.

Total input costs — seed, fertilizer, pesticide, pump electricity, hired labor for maize planting and maybe some cotton picking — I'm figuring about **7,800 yuan**. I have maybe 9,000 yuan cash put aside, so I can cover it, but I won't spend it all. My grandson needs school fees in the fall, and my wife's blood pressure medicine isn't getting cheaper. If fertilizer prices go up again, I might skip the maize topdress and just pray for rain. That's the gamble every year.
